title: Students and staff protest university funding levels in Vienna
seoTitle: Vienna student protest over university funds

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against government plans for higher education funding covering 2028-2030, which fall short of institutional requests.
tea.want: Adequate public funding for higher education and science without cuts to research, teaching, or employment.
tea.changed: Oct 23: Reports detailed turnout figures following the demonstrations held on Thursday.

summary: Thousands of university students, staff, and demonstrators marched through central Vienna on Thursday to protest planned funding levels for higher education and science for 2028-2030. The government confirmed a €16 billion budget for public universities, which is €2 billion short of what institutions requested. Institutions warned the funding gap could cause cuts to research, teaching, and employment, impacting international students and academic progress requirements. The Austrian Students' Union organised the demonstration and estimated turnout at 50,000, while police stated at least 30,000 people attended the rally.
demands: Prevent cuts to higher education and science
Fully fund university requests for the 2028-2030 period
response: No official government response to the protest itself was reported in the sources, though the government confirmed its €16 billion budget plan for public universities.

crowd.text: At least 30,000 people attended the rally, police said.

updates.text: Thousands of students, staff, and demonstrators took to the streets of Vienna to protest higher education funding plans.
Organisers and police released differing crowd estimates ranging from 30,000 to 50,000 participants.
